precepts.text: A host surrounded the city with horses and chariots, and Elisha's servant said, Alas, my master! how shall we do? A whole army came for this one prophet. And he answered, Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them. Elisha prayed, Lord, open his eyes, that he may see: and behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire. Those were angels waiting for the word. You cannot see things spiritually, but understand: the Lord is with us, his angels are with us, and the Lord is fighting with us. There is no way we could do what the Lord sent us to do on this earth, and no way you would see the growth of IUIC and of Israel, if he were not with us. And prepare your mind: it is going to be the same in the future; they came for one prophet, and they will come with agents and lies for those who teach the word of God. Read about COINTELPRO and ask yourself if you think that stopped.
precepts.point: For the battle is not yours, but God's. Why does it say the battle belongs to the Lord? Because the Lord is always there fighting with you.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
“for the battle is not yours, but God’s.” Why does the battle belong to the Lord? Because the Lord is always there fighting with you, even though you cannot see him. Even when you are doing evil, the angels are right there watching and writing down everything you do; the eyes of the Lord are open on all of us. For those who do not believe the Lord is with them and fighting with them, for those with weak faith, look at Elisha.

“And when the servant of the man of God was risen early, and gone forth, behold, an host compassed the city both with horses and chariots. And his servant said unto him, Alas, my master! how shall we do?” A whole army surrounded the city, and they came for this one prophet, this one brother.

“And he answered, Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.” As men of God you have to realize the Lord is always with you, and those with you are stronger than those with the enemy. “And Elisha prayed, and said, Lord, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see. And the Lord opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.” Chariots of fire: angels, just waiting for the word. A man’s army surrounded Elisha, and the Lord’s army surrounded that army, waiting to set it off.

You cannot see things spiritually, but understand: the Lord is with us, his angels are with us, and the Lord is fighting with us. There is no way we could do what the Lord sent us to do on this earth, and no way you would see the growth of IUIC and of Israel, if he were not with us. And it will be the same in the future: they came for one prophet, and federal agents will surround the houses of some of you who teach the word of God. That is the mind you have to have. So be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of the great multitude.

precepts.text: Forasmuch then as Christ hath suffered for us in the flesh, arm yourselves likewise with the same mind. If your mind is not prepared to suffer the same way Christ suffered, you are not a soldier in Christ. The Bible is telling you what is going to happen; do not live in la la land. For he that hath suffered in the flesh hath ceased from sin: that is how you become perfect. Those of you that want a comfortable life, this truth is not for you.
precepts.point: For the battle is not yours, but God's. Why does it say the battle belongs to the Lord? Because the Lord is always there fighting with you.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
Do not be afraid of armies and people; teach the word of God no matter what they threaten you with. You are not going to be a servant of God and have everything be good. You are not going to be a soldier in Christ and not suffer.

“Forasmuch then as Christ hath suffered for us in the flesh, arm yourselves likewise with the same mind”. The same way Christ suffered for us in the flesh, when the Romans crucified him, lynched him and beat him, you have to arm yourself with that same mind. If your mind is not ready to suffer the same way Christ suffered, you are not a soldier in Christ. The Bible is telling you what is going to happen, but some of you are in la-la land.

Eventually an army is going to surround my house, and they are going to lie on me and call me a terrorist or something stupid like that. I already know that is what they will do, so I prepare my mind. Federal agents are waiting to set you up. Do you think the American government is going to let us keep teaching and waking Israel up and just leave us alone? Read about COINTELPRO. Do you think that stopped? We are going up against a wicked, evil people who will put you away for the rest of your life and lie on you, knowing you did not do it, because of the teachings of Christ.

“for he that hath suffered in the flesh hath ceased from sin”. That is how you become perfect: you have to go through things and suffer in the flesh. Those of you who want a comfortable life, this truth is not for you. The battle is the Lord’s, and he fights with us, but we arm our minds to suffer as Christ did.

precepts.text: We have no might against this great company that cometh against us, neither know we what to do, but our eyes are upon thee.
precepts.point: He that remaineth shall be for our God, a governor in Judah, and Ekron as a Jebusite: as David smote the Jebusites and Solomon levied a tribute of bondservice on those left in the land, they will be our servants. No oppressor shall pass through them any more, for now have I seen with mine eyes, as God looked upon the children of Israel and had respect unto them.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.why:
“The burden of the word of the Lord in the land of Hadrach, and Damascus shall be the rest thereof”: this is Syria. And it comes “when the eyes of man, as of all the tribes of Israel, shall be toward the Lord.” All the eyes of Israel, our people, shall be toward the Lord.

2 Chronicles 20:12 has the wording for it: “O our God, wilt thou not judge them? for we have no might against this great company that cometh against us; neither know we what to do: but our eyes are upon thee.” That is what we are saying to the Lord.

The nations are at war around Syria, Lebanon, Gaza and Ashkelon, and we have no might against that great company. We do not know what to do. So we keep our eyes on the Lord, and we have to put our attention toward him. That is the moment Zechariah is speaking of, when the burden of the Lord falls on those lands and all the tribes of Israel look to him.

precepts.text: Judah and Jerusalem went again to Jerusalem with joy, for the Lord had made them to rejoice over their enemies. God made us to rejoice over our enemies when the battle was won.
precepts.point: Rome, you just slaughtered a thousand Israelites, let me pray for you, is the stupidest thought there is, and it is the idea the black Christian holds and preaches.

precepts.text: Be not afraid by reason of this great multitude; the battle is not yours, but God's.
precepts.point: The victory of battle stands not in the multitude of an host; strength comes from heaven. Whether with many or with them that have no power, the battle is not yours but God's; our forefathers proved it, as when Asa cried to the Lord and a million Ethiopians fell before Judah and Benjamin.

note.label: Genesis 14: The War of the Kings and Melchizedek

precepts.why:
The word to Judah facing a great multitude is the word behind Abram’s victory: “Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s.”

Abram “heard that his brother was taken captive” and went after four kings with three hundred and eighteen trained servants. Whether with many or with few, the battle is not yours but God’s, and that is why he smote them and “brought back all the goods, and also brought again his brother Lot.”

precepts.why: Armageddon is coming; you have heard about it since you were a child, but it is soon to come. We won't have to fight in this upcoming war, just like Jehoshaphat did not have to fight when he was at war. Watch what God said to Jehoshaphat. “And he said, Hearken ye, all Judah, and ye inhabitants of Jerusalem,” That is the elect. “and thou king Jehoshaphat, Thus saith the Lord unto you,” What he says to him right here he is saying to us too. “Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude;” Don't be afraid or dismayed of the multitude of nations. “for the battle is not yours,” The battle is not ours, brothers and sisters, “but God’s.”

moments.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, joined himself with Ahaziah, king of Israel, who did very wickedly. Then Eliezer prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, because thou hast joined thyself with Ahaziah, the Lord hath broken thy works. And listen, we doing mighty works: all praises for good leadership, all praises for our bishops, our deacons, all praises for those who labor in Christ before us. But it's telling you that if we join with those who doing wickedness, the Lord will break our works. And the ships were broken, that they were not able to go to Tarshish.

They saying, oh, we got to scrap affirmative action, we got to scrap EBT, when white people, even Amalek, the tiny hat, one of the most prominent consumers of EBT. But all this is why: because this whole country, this whole system is designed off of our bloodshed and our suffering. We the fuel to keep the whole system running: our blood and bones.

Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude. Do not be scared of armies and people, brothers and sisters. Teach the word of God, speak the word of God, no matter what they say or what they threaten you with.
For the battle is not yours, but God's. Why does it say the battle belongs to the Lord? Because the Lord is always there fighting with you.
